title: الفصل الثاني من الباب الخامس في صفة قلم كوكب المشتري وهيته كما تري فافهم
titleNote: Transcribed as printed, in three lines, without added hamzas; the print sets a small mark over the ه of وهيته, and كما تري is set close together.
titleParaphrase: Second section of the fifth chapter: on the form of the pen (script) of the planet al-Mushtarī (Jupiter), and its shape, as you see; so understand. Paraphrase by the tracer, not a quotation of any translation.
headingHammer: CHAPTER V. The Alphabets of the Seven Planets. … SECTION II. The alphabet of Jupiter, (v. orig. p. 48.)
headingHammerLocator: Hammer's English part, p. [10] (leaf 40 of the scan, b22039910_0040.jp2), read on the leaf by the tracer.

primary.copy: Wellcome Library copy, digitised for the Internet Archive as item b22039910 (rights field: Creative Commons Public Domain Mark, as recorded in plates/ibn-wahshiyya.manifest.json).
primary.work: Joseph Hammer (ed. and trans.), Ancient Alphabets and Hieroglyphic Characters Explained (London: W. Bulmer and Co., 1806): the Arabic text of Shawq al-mustahām, Bāb V, faṣl 2, the pen of the planet Jupiter (al-Mushtarī).
primary.locator: Arabic part, p. 48 (printed "48" and, at the other corner, the Arabic numeral ٤٨ in the Persian form of the 4), the one table on the page, under its heading; leaf 175 of the scan (b22039910_0175.jp2), Internet Archive page n174. The book's Arabic part is paginated from the back, so in the scan Arabic p. 48 is leaf 175.
primary.plate: plates/ibn-wahshiyya/jupiter/table.png (an exact pixel copy of leaf 175 at offset 240, 1070: checked, zero difference); the cells were cut from b22039910_0175.jp2 itself.
primary.urlCheck: Both URLs fetched by the tracer on 2026-10-20 (HTTP 200). The page image (2093 x 2896 px) matches leaf 175 of the JP2 set (greyscale correlation 0.999; against a different leaf 0.08).
primary.valuesPrinted: yes: an Arabic letter is printed under each sign; every one is legible.

layout: Four rows read from right to left: 8 signs (ا to ح), 8 (ط to ع), 8 (ف ص ق ر ش ت ث خ) and 4 (ذ ض ظ غ) centred. Small round separator dots stand between the signs; they are not part of any sign and are not drawn.
cellSize: One cell size for the whole table: a 168 px square cut from the leaf (300 ppi), centred on the sign's ink, upscaled x3 (Lanczos) to 504 px. 1 glyph unit = 1.68 leaf px. Separator dots and bits of the Arabic letters below show at the edges of some cells.
tracing: Centre lines traced over a skeleton of the inked strokes (threshold 118 of 255 on the greyscale leaf) and checked by overlay. Ring-ends are drawn as kit rings (radius 6 unless noted) placed on the printed ring, with the stroke stopping on the ring's edge where the print joins it.
ringsAndBalls: Ring or ball was decided first by measuring the brightest point near the middle of each round end on the Wellcome leaf, as a share of the way from ink (about 30) to paper (about 183): open rings read 70 percent or more, filled balls 4 to 29 percent; then every round end was looked for in the Getty and UNC copies, and an opening found at the same place in both of them was taken as an opening in the printing. Borderline ends are named in the notes of their signs. The task brief expected filled balls in ا, ف and the ظ/غ forms: ا has one (top right, solid in all three copies), ف one (lower left; its lower right end, solid in the Wellcome copy, shows an opening in the other two and is drawn as a ring), خ one (at the foot; its upper end is a ring), and س two (lower ends); in ظ and غ every round end is an open ring (78 to 97 percent), and the right-hand points of ظ are sharp corners, not balls.
variantsNote: Checked against two further copies of the 1806 printing: the Getty Research Institute copy (Internet Archive ancientalphabets01ibnw, page n176) and the University of North Carolina copy (ancientalphabets00ibnw, page n53). 27 of the 28 signs have the same form in the three copies. In ط the Wellcome copy lacks the right-hand side that the other two print, and the sign is drawn from them (see its note). Two round ends that are filled in the Wellcome copy show openings in the other two and are drawn as rings (the upper end of خ, the lower right end of ف). The two Oxford copies scanned by Google and the BSB scan listed in plates/ibn-wahshiyya.manifest.json were not compared, and no manuscript was consulted.

letters.strokes: three strokes: an upright on the right topped by a heavy filled ball; a diagonal from just under the ball down to the lower left, ending in a ring; and a long stroke from a foot at the lower middle up across the diagonal to a rounded apex at the upper left, which turns back down as the other side of a narrow loop and meets the diagonal just above the ring
letters.note: The ball at the top right is solid (11 percent on the ring-or-ball measure). The ring at the lower left is open (88 percent).

letters.name: ṭāʾ
letters.strokes: a box open on the left (like ⊐) with a ring at each left-hand end: the top ring hangs below the end of the top bar, the bottom ring sits above the end of the bottom bar
letters.note: The copies disagree. In the Wellcome copy only the two bars with their rings are printed, and both bars stop short (the upper at about x 68, the lower at about x 73, with a faint speck near the lower right corner); the right-hand side is missing. The Getty and UNC copies of the same printing both show the right-hand side closing the box, so the sign is drawn from them, and its cell is the Getty copy (ancientalphabets01ibnw, page n176) cut in the same frame as the Wellcome cells (the Wellcome cell is kept as cellWellcome). Why the side is missing in the Wellcome copy (inking or damage) cannot be told. The rings and the left half agree in all three copies. Drawn this way the sign is the left-right mirror of the next sign, ي.

letters.name: ẓāʾ
letters.strokes: an upright on the left with a ring at each end; from the upper ring a bar runs right to a point, turns back to a point in the middle (like <), out again to a second point at the right, and back along the bottom to the lower ring
letters.note: The two right-hand points are sharp corners, heavy where the lines meet, not balls. Both rings are open (78 percent at the top and 94 percent at the foot on the ring-or-ball measure).

letters.strokes: three parallel strokes falling to the right, crossed by two short parallel bars rising to the right, each running from the left stroke over the middle one to the right stroke; the left and right strokes end below in rings, the middle one in a plain end
letters.note: The top of the left stroke has a small hook to the left. Both lower rings are open (94 and 97 percent on the ring-or-ball measure).

otherCopies.method: Each page image was registered onto the Wellcome leaf (SIFT features on the table, similarity transform fitted with RANSAC; scale about 1.24 to 1.26, rotation under half a degree), each Wellcome cell frame was mapped into it and refined by a local correlation search (shifts of 0 to 3 units; correlation 0.94 to 0.98 except where the sign itself differs), so the cells of all three copies share the glyph frame. The page images were fetched on 2026-10-20 and kept outside the site; they serve only as witnesses.

check.summary: Every sign compared with the Wellcome print and with the Getty and UNC copies, registered onto the same cells: label and order, strokes, joins, direction, ends, rings and balls, and proportion. Corrected: ط (redrawn as a closed ⊐ from the Getty and UNC copies; the Wellcome copy lacks its right-hand side), خ (upper end a ring, not a ball), ف (lower right end a ring, not a ball); notes of ز and س extended with the other copies' evidence.
